description: Multi-hop campus graph conversations. Each answer needs two or more connected facts, such as program to convener to contact. run.py sends them to the Brain like any other corpus; check_graph_paths.py checks each case's declared graph path against a published graph export without model calls. Expected facts come from the snapshot below and can go stale as events pass and sources change.

phases.title: Archway organizer groups as organization identities
Program requirement groups as contextual records with explicit course options
Program to listed faculty from the catalog's explicit Program Faculty field
People and offices to buildings from published room numbers
Programs and people to schools through a reviewed name mapping
Reviewed aliases, including deliberately ambiguous ones

graph.leaf: The person's own contact record: sfrees@ramapo.edu, office ASB-409.

expected_behaviors: Follow the catalog Convener-field relationship from the program to the person, then use that person's own contact record.

turns.user: Who is the convener of the Computer Science BS program?
expected_behaviors: Name Scott Frees and attribute it to the catalog's Convener field. Do not present it as a verified current appointment beyond what the catalog states.
Resolve 'their' to Scott Frees and give sfrees@ramapo.edu and office ASB-409 from his contact record, not from the program record.

graph.note: Reachable in chat through lookup_profile's related section (relationship convener, direction incoming) since Brain 4511572.

messages.content: Which programs does Professor Emma C. Rainforth convene?

expected_behaviors: List the five programs whose catalog Convener field names her: Environmental Science BS, Natural Sciences BS, Earth Science Minor, Environmental Science Minor and Science and Society Minor. Do not add programs from her department or her course list.

messages.content: Which courses are listed on the faculty profile of the Music BA convener?

expected_behaviors: Identify Christopher Reali from the catalog Convener field, then list the six catalog courses coded on his faculty profile: MUSI 232, 249, 263, 301, 336 and 350. Present them as an undated profile list, not his current teaching schedule.
Follow the event's explicit organizer link to the club, then back to the club's other linked events.

turns.user: Who is organizing Gratitude Journals on October 8, 2026, and how do I contact them?
expected_behaviors: Name Psychology Affiliation from the event page's explicit organizer, and give psychaf@ramapo.edu from the club's own directory record.

turns.user: What else are they hosting in November 2026?
expected_behaviors: List Psychology Grad Panel (November 5, 1-2 PM) and Discovering Personality (November 19, 1-2 PM). Say this covers events with an approved organizer link, not the complete campus calendar.

messages.content: What events does the Sports Club have in October 2026?

expected_behaviors: Select the October occurrences among the club's linked events: Falcons VS Saints (October 5, 8-10 PM), Bills VS Rams (October 12, 1-2 PM), Commanders VS 49ers (October 19, 8-10 PM) and Cowboys VS Eagles (October 26, 8-10 PM). Keep each occurrence's own time, exclude September, November and December dates, and do not call the result the complete campus calendar.

messages.content: Is Emma C. Rainforth teaching Geology of New Jersey (GEOL 327) this semester?

expected_behaviors: Her faculty profile lists GEOL 327, but the list is undated. Say the evidence does not establish that she teaches it this semester, rather than answering yes or no.

graph.note: The programs artifact still carries a legacy first-listed-faculty convener (Constance Crawford); it must never become an edge or an answer.

messages.content: Who is the convener of the Accounting BS program?

expected_behaviors: The catalog has no Convener-field link for this program. Do not name Constance Crawford, or anyone else, as convener from the legacy first-listed-faculty fallback. Say the convener is not published and point to available program resources instead.

messages.content: What courses are required for the Computer Science BS?

expected_behaviors: Separate required courses from choices. Required: CMPS 147, 148, 220, 231, 311, 361, 366 and 450, MATH 121, and one of MATH 205 or MATH 237. Choices: at least 2 of the 17 Math Electives options and at least 7 of the 18 Computer Science Electives options, plus the Career Pathway requirements and General Education. Never list elective options as required courses.

graph.note: Starting from the program's own Math Electives group ties the options to that group, not to any Computer Science BS requirement.

messages.content: How many math electives do I need for the Computer Science BS, and what are the options?

expected_behaviors: At least 2 from the Math Electives group, which has 17 options: MATH 122, 124, 200, 225, 240, 245, 253, 262, 282, 290, 300, 305, 321, 339, 360 and 390, plus MATH 353 or MATH 370 as a single option. Keep the count attached to the group.

messages.content: Is CMPS 331 Artificial Intelligence required for the Computer Science BS?

expected_behaviors: No. It is one of 18 options in the CS BS group 'Computer Science Electives: Select Seven (7)', from which students choose at least seven. Appearing in a program's requirements does not make a course required.
Keep requirement groups scoped to the program the student asked about.

turns.user: Is Data Structures required for the Computer Science minor?
expected_behaviors: Yes: CMPS 231 Data Structures is in the minor's Required Courses, along with CMPS 147 and CMPS 148.

For the minor, CMPS 311 Operating Systems is only one of 20 elective options, of which students choose at least 3. It is required for the CS BS, not the minor; do not carry the major's requirement over.

messages.content: Which programs require CMPS 147 Computer Science I?

expected_behaviors: Separate required from alternatives. Required outright: Computer Science BS, Cybersecurity BS, Engineering Physics BS and the Computer Science Minor. Mathematics BS (both tracks) requires CMPS 130 or CMPS 147. Biology BS lists it as one option in its Math Requirement (choose at least 2). It is also a General Education Quantitative Reasoning option. Do not flatten the alternatives into 'required'.

graph.note: 64 programs carry this identical block; it should be one shared group, not 64 copies.

messages.content: Which courses satisfy the General Education Quantitative Reasoning requirement?

expected_behaviors: Choose one of CMPS 110, CMPS 147, MATH 100T, MATH 101, MATH 104, MATH 106, MATH 108, MATH 110, MATH 121 or PHIL 106. Include the catalog note that a major may specify a particular math course. Present it as the shared General Education requirement, not one program's requirement.

graph.note: Only the catalog's explicit Program Faculty field (customFields.xiQxl) is evidence. The published faculty array mixes fields, name matches and, for some programs, a scraper heuristic.

Yeaton (kyeaton@ramapo.edu), each email from that person's own record. Describe them as listed program faculty, not as teaching particular courses this term.

messages.content: Is Constance Crawford the convener of the Accounting BS, or is she just on its faculty?

expected_behaviors: The catalog lists her in the program's Program Faculty field, but no Convener-field evidence names a convener for this program. Say she is listed faculty and the convener is not published; do not promote her to convener because she is listed first.
Carry the subject across three turns: program to convener, convener to office room, room to building.

turns.user: Who is the convener of the Finance BS?
expected_behaviors: Name Timothy Haase from the catalog Convener field.
Give room ASB-511 from Timothy Haase's own contact record.
The Anisfield School of Business (ASB) building, from the reviewed room-prefix mapping. A building is a location, not a claim about which school he belongs to.

messages.content: Which building is the Registrar in, and which other offices in the campus directory are in that building?

expected_behaviors: The Registrar's room D-224 places it in Academic Building D. Other directory offices with D-wing rooms: Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) D-207, Counseling Center D-216 and Health Services D-216C. Say this covers offices with published room numbers, not a complete building directory.

expect.name: School of Science, Nursing, and Health

messages.content: Which school is the Computer Science BS in, and is its convener in the same school?

expected_behaviors: The program record lists the School of Theoretical and Applied Science; Scott Frees's faculty profile lists the School of Science, Nursing, and Health. Report both with their sources. Without a reviewed mapping between the older and newer school names, do not claim they are the same school or different ones.

messages.content: Who convenes Computer Science?

expected_behaviors: 'Computer Science' matches four programs: the BS, MS, Minor and 4+1. Either ask which one, or say the catalog lists Scott Frees as convener of all four, citing each. Do not silently answer for the BS alone.
